description_full: Bravura Solutions Limited provides software solutions for the wealth management and transfer agency industries in Australia, the United Kingdom, New Zealand, and internationally. The company offers Babel, a network of fund transaction networks; Rufus, a digital-first transfer agency platform for asset managers and asset servicers; Dashboards Connect, an ISP for pensions dashboards program; ePASS, a digital employee contribution processing system; Garradin, a trade execution, portfolio management, and asset servicing platform; Orchestrator, a workflow automation platform; Midwinter Advice, a digital (hybrid) and comprehensive advice; Sonata, a wealth management technology; Sonata Alta, a digital-first business model; taWeb, a configurable, self-service investor portal; and Wealth microservices, which provides an open architecture and regulatory microservices. It also provides professional consulting services for the wealth management and funds administration sectors of the financial services industry. In addition, the company offers wrap platforms, superannuation and pension, private wealth and portfolio administration, financial planning software, and unit registry. It offers its solutions for wealth and retirement, advice, life insurance, funds services, and integration and automation sectors. The company was formerly known as Bravura Solutions Holdings Pty Ltd and changed its name to Bravura Solutions Limited in October 2016. Bravura Solutions Limited was founded in 2004 and is headquartered in Sydney, Australia.

financial_summary: Bravura Solutions Ltd. is a small-cap technology business with a $471M market cap on $194M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +14.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 31% against a 8% cost of capital — a 23-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 100% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $54M in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 12.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 26% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
